alt: One mock contest logged on a 0 to 180 minute line with a row for each problem. Each bar is one stretch of work ending in a submission: OK for accepted, WA for wrong answer, or an open bar where the clock ran out before a submission. A problem with several bars took several submissions.

steps.caption: Minutes 0 to 10 went to reading the statements. Then minute 10 to 38, problem 1. One stretch, and the submission is accepted. That is 28 minutes in stretches so far.
Minute 38 to 70, problem 2. The submission gets wrong answer. That is 60 minutes in stretches so far.
Minute 70 to 85, problem 2. Another submission, and it gets wrong answer again. That is 75 minutes in stretches so far.
Minute 85 to 130, problem 3. The submission gets wrong answer. That is 120 minutes in stretches so far.
Minute 130 to 152, problem 2. This is its third stretch, and the submission is accepted. That is 142 minutes in stretches so far.
Minute 152 to 180, problem 4. The clock runs out before any submission, so the bar ends open. That is 170 minutes in stretches so far.
The finished log has one row per problem; a row with several bars took several submissions. Problems 3 and 4 were never accepted, so they come first when upsolving.

Minute 30 to 60, problem 2. One stretch, and the submission is accepted. That is 50 minutes in stretches so far.
Minute 60 to 95, problem 3. One stretch, and the submission is accepted. That is 85 minutes in stretches so far.
Minute 95 to 140, problem 4. One stretch, and the submission is accepted. That is 130 minutes in stretches so far.
The finished log has one row per problem; a row with several bars took several submissions. Every problem attempted is accepted, and minutes 140 to 180 went unused.
